Creates a new IM channel for the org. Required fields are name and integrationServiceId. Optional fields include configParams (integration-specific credentials), meta, defaultBotId, isSandBox. If isSandBox is omitted, it defaults to false.

For WhatsApp production channels, obtain the PHONE_NUMBER value for configParams by calling GET /api/v1/im/integrationServices/WHATSAPP/details to list WABA accounts, then GET /api/v1/im/integrationServices/WHATSAPP/phonenumbers with query parameter wabaId to list phone numbers for the chosen WABA. If these APIs return no data, complete Facebook embedded signup from the Desk UI before retrying channel creation.

After creation, associate the channel with a Desk department using PATCH /api/v1/im/channels/id/department.

That subscription end-point must return a 200 OK message to confirm the subscription. If the 200 OK message is not received, a validation POST request is initiated to the subscription URL. Failure to receive a 200 OK message will result in the failure of webhook creation.

toUuid.description: Canvas anchor UUID for the incoming endpoint of the destination state on the designer. Type: string. Required. This is not the state ID; it is a visual port identifier used only by chartData.connectionDetails. Pattern: state name followed by a unique numeric suffix (for example, "On Hold1", "Closed1"). Each connection endpoint must use its own anchor UUID. Do not reuse the same UUID as both the incoming anchor (toUuid) and outgoing anchor (fromUuid) on the same state. Example: for Open -> On Hold -> Closed, use toUuid "On Hold1" on the first connection and fromUuid "On Hold2" (not "On Hold1") on the second connection.

transName.description: Name of the transition for the connection

isCommTrans.description: Indicates whether the connection is a common transition. Possible values: @true@ - connection is a common transition, @false@ - connection is a specific transition

fromUuid.description: Canvas anchor UUID for the outgoing endpoint of the source state on the designer. Type: string. Required. This is not the state ID; it is a visual port identifier used only by chartData.connectionDetails. Pattern: state name followed by a unique numeric suffix (for example, "Open0", "On Hold2"). Each connection endpoint must use its own anchor UUID. When a state has both incoming and outgoing connections, assign different suffixes for each port (for example, incoming toUuid "On Hold1" and outgoing fromUuid "On Hold2"). Reusing one anchor for both directions prevents the designer from rendering the second connection.

toUuid.description: Canvas anchor UUID for the incoming endpoint of the destination state on the designer. Type: string. Required. This is not the state ID; it is a visual port identifier used only by chartData.connectionDetails. Pattern: state name followed by a unique numeric suffix (for example, "On Hold1", "Closed1"). Each connection endpoint must use its own anchor UUID. Do not reuse the same UUID as both the incoming anchor (toUuid) and outgoing anchor (fromUuid) on the same state. Example: for Open -> On Hold -> Closed, use toUuid "On Hold1" on the first connection and fromUuid "On Hold2" (not "On Hold1") on the second connection.

fromUuid.description: Canvas anchor UUID for the outgoing endpoint of the source state on the designer. Type: string. Required. This is not the state ID; it is a visual port identifier used only by chartData.connectionDetails. Pattern: state name followed by a unique numeric suffix (for example, "Open0", "On Hold2"). Each connection endpoint must use its own anchor UUID. When a state has both incoming and outgoing connections, assign different suffixes for each port (for example, incoming toUuid "On Hold1" and outgoing fromUuid "On Hold2"). Reusing one anchor for both directions prevents the designer from rendering the second connection.

value.answer:
Zoho Desk packs a bunch of features that are expressly there to help you respond to tickets smartly.

The first of these, you've already discovered: Auto-Suggest Articles. Zoho Desk pulls up relevant articles on the ticket's content—so you can save time on frequently asked questions.

Every action that you can perform with respect to a ticket has a corresponding keyboard shortcut. With these, you can optimize the time you spend on each ticket. (And the shortcut to access these shortcuts is Shift + ? ).When you need to quickly consult a colleague, you can tag them in a ticket comment without having to leave this screen. That's like a quick chat, without even leaving your place, and with the full context of the ticket.

With these, you're good to go.

Go on, save the world from bad customer service!
